## 📖 Welcome to Los Santos, Where Promises Die Fast.

Los Santos is no place for honest people; it is a city built on empty promises, impossible credit and overblown aspirations. This guide is your road map for getting around San Andreas, where the difference between making it big and ending up in the morgue often comes down to who drives faster and who shoots first.

### 👥 Three Protagonists: Three Ways of Getting Into Trouble

**Franklin Clinton** wants more. Used to making his way through the streets of Los Santos, he aspires to leave behind a life that seems to have a future far too small prepared for him. He has ambition, instinct and a drive to get ahead, even though the opportunities that come his way don't always come from the most recommendable people.

---

**Michael De Santa** seems to have achieved what many are chasing: a nice house, money and a comfortable life in the hills of Los Santos. Behind that apparent calm, however, lie a dysfunctional family, a past that never quite disappears and a dissatisfaction that not even the best neighborhood can hide. Some people dream of retiring. Michael is proof that retiring and finding peace are two very different things.

---

**Trevor Philips**, for his part, lives by rules that would probably not survive a neighborhood association meeting. Impulsive, violent and unpredictable, he is capable of turning an ordinary situation into a problem of considerable proportions. But reducing him to his temper would be staying on the surface: Trevor has his own idea of loyalty, of friendship and of how things should be done. Whether those ideas are reassuring for the rest of humanity is another matter.

---

Three men, three circumstances and three ways of understanding the world. Their paths will cross in a story marked by ambitions, old unfinished business, tested loyalties and decisions whose consequences rarely stay where they should.

---

### 🎬 The Story Starts Here

GTA V's story mode invites you to travel across San Andreas through these three protagonists, each with their own personality, their relationships and their own problems. As you progress, you will discover their stories, meet the people who are part of their lives and find yourself caught up in situations that go far beyond a simple job.

---

And when you aren't following the main thread, the city will still be there. Its roads, its neighborhoods, its landscapes and its secrets don't disappear just because you have a pending mission. There will always be something to discover, a place to return to or a decision that might have been better thought through twice.

---

This guide will accompany you along that journey: from the first steps of the story to its most important moments, with information about the protagonists, the missions and the places that make San Andreas much more than a backdrop.

## 🕶️ Michael De Santa

### 🌆 The American Dream, With a Criminal Record

Some people spend half their lives trying to escape their past. **Michael De Santa** managed to change his last name, move to one of the most exclusive areas of Los Santos and buy himself a mansion with a pool. On paper, it looks like the operation was a complete success. The small drawback is that changing your identity turns out to be quite a bit easier than changing who you are.

Before becoming the well-off Rockford Hills resident we meet at the beginning of GTA V, Michael was Michael Townley: a professional criminal with experience in heists, a difficult temper and a track record that was hardly among the recommended role models for young people.

His current life is the result of a radical decision: to leave the criminal world and start over. Or, at least, to try to convince everyone —himself included— that this is what he has done.

---

### 🏈 From the Football Fields to the Heists

Michael's childhood was far from the privileges he would later offer his own children. He grew up in a humble environment, marked by family problems and a difficult relationship with his father, whom the game's references describe as an abusive alcoholic. He didn't have an especially easy life and, from a young age, seemed to find it harder to build a stable future than to get into trouble.

During his teenage years he stood out playing American football. He became the quarterback of a state-level team and had the chance to imagine a future far from the margins of society. However, injuries and his temper problems ended up frustrating those aspirations.

Sport didn't end up becoming the career he had imagined. Crime, on the other hand, did offer him a much longer-lasting professional path.

Michael began to build up experience in the criminal world and ended up becoming a competent bank robber, a good shot with the ability to organize complex operations. He wasn't simply someone willing to pick up a gun: he also knew how to plan, assess risks and work with other criminals.

Among those relationships, the one he had with Trevor Philips stood out. Together they took part in various heists and developed a partnership that went far beyond sharing a job. There was trust, history and a dangerous familiarity, the kind that is only built when several people have had to depend on each other in situations where a mistake can cost them their lives.

But Michael began to contemplate a possibility that didn't fit very well with that existence: leaving it all behind.

---

### 🎬 Amanda, Jimmy and Tracey: A Picture-Perfect Family

At some point in his criminal career, Michael met Amanda, who worked as a dancer in a club. The relationship grew into marriage and the two started a family with their two children, Jimmy and Tracey.

Michael wanted something different for them. He didn't want them to grow up in the same circumstances he did, amid precariousness, crime and the uncertainty of not knowing what would come next. He wanted to offer them safety, stability and opportunities. In other words, he wanted to give them what he felt he had been missing during his own childhood.

The irony is that, years later, he would end up living in a luxury mansion while watching his family seem determined to turn that aspiration into a rather questionable social experiment.

Amanda has her own interests, her own frustrations and an increasingly complicated relationship with her husband. Money, shopping, infidelities and arguments are part of a life together in which appearances matter almost as much as the problems they try to hide.

Jimmy, his son, spends a good part of his time among video games and with an attitude that doesn't exactly help improve the relationship with his father. Michael thinks the boy is wasting his opportunities; Jimmy, for his part, doesn't seem especially interested in accepting life lessons from a man whose résumé includes heists and violent crimes.

Tracey, his daughter, chases fame and dreams of making her way in the world of entertainment. Her aspirations lead her into situations that worry Michael, although his attempts to protect her are not always especially effective.

The De Santa family is, in short, an exaggerated but recognizable portrait of a society obsessed with money, success and public image. Everyone wants something, everyone has their flaws and almost everyone seems convinced that the main problem in the house is someone else.

Michael isn't left out of that equation either. His character, his egocentrism, his infidelities and his tendency to impose his own expectations contribute to the deterioration of life at home. Paying for a nice house and filling the fridge isn't enough to become father of the year. Although, judging by some of their family arguments, perhaps being right isn't enough either.

---

### 🍸 Rockford Hills: The Reward That Doesn't Quite Work

When GTA V begins, Michael lives in a mansion in Rockford Hills, surrounded by comforts and with a financial situation that many would consider enviable.

He has managed to escape his old life, at least in appearance. He has a spectacular house, a pool, cars and free time. He doesn't need to get up every morning to clock in at an office or worry about making ends meet.

And yet, he is deeply dissatisfied.

Michael spends a good part of his days among alcohol, television, action movies and domestic arguments. The life he imagined as a reward for leaving crime behind has turned into a routine he finds suffocating.

Here appears one of the most interesting contradictions of the character. Michael wanted to leave danger behind, but he also misses the intensity of his old life. He wanted to be present for his family, but doesn't always know how to relate to them. He wanted peace and quiet, yet seems unable to enjoy it now that he finally has it.

It is as if he had spent so many years preparing to escape that he never stopped to think about what he was going to do once he succeeded.

And Los Santos, a city that sells success as if it were a luxury product, turns out to be the perfect setting for that crisis. Michael lives surrounded by the symbols of a successful life, but none of them seems to provide the satisfaction he expected.

---

### 🛋️ The Man Who Goes to the Therapist

One of Michael's most singular characteristics is his relationship with Dr. Isiah Friedlander, the psychologist he visits to deal with his personal problems.

The sessions offer some of the most revealing moments of the character. Michael talks about his family, his frustration and his inability to find meaning in the life he has built. He is good at identifying other people's flaws, but a lot less at examining his own without resorting to a justification.

Friedlander, for his part, isn't portrayed as an infallible professional either. His practice and the relationship he has with Michael serve to introduce a satire of therapy, money and the industry that turns personal difficulties into a paid service.

Michael can spend an entire session talking about how miserable he feels and leave without having resolved much. Of course, the bill for the session will probably arrive on time.

Beneath the humor there is something more important: Michael knows his life doesn't work, but acknowledging it doesn't mean he is willing to change the decisions that brought him here. He has explanations for almost everything and a remarkable ability to find someone to blame. What he is less sure about is what to do with himself.

---

### 🤝 Trevor Philips: The Past That Didn't Stay Behind

The relationship between Michael and Trevor is one of the fundamental pieces of GTA V.

They shared a long criminal career and took part in heists that cemented their reputation. Trevor is impulsive, unpredictable and much harder to restrain; Michael is calculating, manipulative and, at least in appearance, more aware of the consequences.

However, that difference in character never stopped them from working together. Between them there was a relationship built on shared experiences, loyalties and a familiarity that could be as valuable as it was dangerous.

The problem is that Michael began to want a different life. Starting a family and looking for a way out of the criminal world changed his priorities, but it also led him to make decisions that would have lasting consequences.

Their past was marked by the events of Ludendorff, in North Yankton. What happened there is an essential piece for understanding Michael's story, his secrets and the relationship he has with Trevor.

This is not just two former partners meeting again. It is two men who remember very differently a story they shared and have still not finished resolving.

For Michael, starting over meant leaving a part of his life behind. For Trevor, some things aren't forgotten so easily. And when their paths cross again, it becomes clear that changing city and last name doesn't guarantee that unsettled scores will disappear.

---

### 🎭 Michael Townley vs. Michael De Santa

At heart, Michael lives divided between two identities.

Michael Townley represents the past: the criminal who found in heists a way of making a living and who ended up making a decision that altered his relationship with the people closest to him.

Michael De Santa represents the attempt to start over: the husband, the father and the owner of a mansion that should symbolize that everything has turned out well.

The problem is that both versions belong to the same man.

Michael cannot erase his earlier decisions simply because he now has a pool. Nor can he solve his family problems by treating them as a nuisance interrupting the movie he had imagined for his life.

As the story advances, circumstances force him to face the consequences of his past and to reconsider what it really means to have gotten a second chance.

Because Michael can be intelligent, have experience and know how to handle himself in dangerous situations. What he doesn't always know is how to stop complicating his life when, for once, nobody is pointing a gun at him.

And that is perhaps the great paradox of Michael De Santa: he survived a criminal career, managed to escape it and achieved the dream of living surrounded by comforts. Now he has to figure out why, after all that, he still doesn't feel at peace.

In Los Santos, even the American dream can turn into a nightmare. Especially when the man trying to enjoy it is unable to stop being who he was.

## 🚗 Franklin Clinton

### A Guy Who Wants to Get Somewhere

**Franklin Clinton** was born in 1988 in South Los Santos, a city that sells opportunities in its ads and offers a much more complicated interpretation of them when you grow up far from the mansions of Vinewood Hills.

His childhood was marked by the absence of his father and the early loss of his mother. After living with his grandparents, he ended up at the home of his aunt Denise, in Strawberry. There he grew up surrounded by an environment in which gangs, petty crime and the pursuit of quick money were part of the everyday landscape.

Franklin wasn't born with a master plan to become a professional criminal. His path took shape among bad decisions, bad influences and an environment in which getting ahead could mean many things, although not all of them led to the same place. The city was full of people who aspired to improve their lives; some wanted to succeed in business, others to become famous and others simply to get enough money to stop worrying about the next bill. Franklin wanted more than to survive, even though he still wasn't very clear on how to achieve it.

---

### 🤝 Lamar Davis: Friendship and Other Obstacles to Getting Ahead

In his youth, Franklin became friends with Lamar Davis. They shared a neighborhood, experiences and a background tied to street gangs. They also shared the kind of trust that lets you tell a friend exactly what you think of him, even when nobody has asked.

Franklin and Lamar are not as different as they sometimes seem, but there is an important difference between them. Lamar feels comfortable inside his world and retains considerable enthusiasm for its codes, its rivalries and its possibilities. Franklin, on the other hand, begins to look around and wonder whether that is really all that awaits him.

It's not that Franklin has suddenly become a model of prudence. He is still involved in shady business, has limited patience for nonsense and doesn't seem especially interested in earning the recognition of a good-manners committee. But he begins to distinguish between making a living and spending his life repeating the same mistakes.

Lamar, for his part, has an extraordinary ability to turn any conversation into a display of personal confidence. Sometimes that self-assurance is useful; other times, you start to suspect that the difference between the two doesn't lie in who has the better ideas, but in who realizes first that an idea is terrible.

Their friendship will be one of Franklin's most important relationships. Also one of the most constant proofs that changing your life can be hard when your old friends consider any sensible decision to be an opportunity to remind you that you are getting boring.

---

### 🚦 The Street Is Not a Career Path

Before the story of *Grand Theft Auto V* begins, Franklin has already accumulated enough trouble to understand that a life of crime has its drawbacks. His time in high school ends with his expulsion after assaulting a teacher. Later he gets involved in crimes and activities related to the gangs of Los Santos.

There's no need to embellish his record too much: Franklin is not a misunderstood saint. He has made decisions that got him into trouble and has willingly taken part in a dangerous environment. But he isn't someone who finds any special satisfaction in staying trapped in the same position forever, either.

The street has taught him to drive, to handle himself in complicated situations and to recognize when someone is trying to take advantage of him. These are skills that, in another context, could have opened considerably more respectable doors for him. In Los Santos, however, career guidance seems to consist of knowing the right person and hoping he doesn't end up owing you money.

Franklin is getting tired of that dynamic. He wants to get ahead, earn money and access a life that doesn't constantly depend on who controls a corner or who has a problem with whom. The drawback is that leaving a way of life isn't as easy as announcing it. Especially when the available alternatives aren't exactly known for their stability either.

---

### 💔 Tanisha: Wanting to Change Doesn't Always Come in Time

Tanisha Jackson was an important person in Franklin's life. Their relationship deteriorated because of his ties to the criminal world and because of the consequences that life could have for those who stayed close. The death of Tanisha's brother, related to gang violence, contributed to driving them apart.

Tanisha represents a possibility that Franklin failed to hold on to: that of building a life away from the street. It doesn't mean she has all the answers or that Franklin can solve his problems simply by following her advice. It means that someone who truly knows him sees the risks of his path and isn't willing to pretend everything will turn out fine.

Franklin wants to move forward, but he is still learning that good intentions don't erase earlier decisions. Nor do they oblige others to wait indefinitely while you decide what you want to do with your life.

In a city where everyone promises to reinvent themselves, Franklin begins to discover that changing course takes more than wishing for a different destiny.

---

### 🚘 Simeon Yetarian: An Honest Job, More or Less

When *Grand Theft Auto V* begins, Franklin works alongside Lamar for Simeon Yetarian, owner of Premium Deluxe Motorsport. His task consists of recovering vehicles from customers who haven't kept up with the agreed payments.

On paper, it looks like a fairly conventional job. There is a boss, a more or less recognizable schedule and a specific task. It might even seem that Franklin has found a way to channel his experience into something resembling a steady job.

Then you remember that Simeon's business consists of selling cars through abusive financing deals and that his employees have to go and get them back when things turn out the way anyone could have expected. The commercial activity has its charm: first you convince someone they can afford a vehicle and then you send Franklin to check in person just how true that claim was.

Simeon is a Los Santos businessman in its purest form. His talent lies in presenting a dubious operation as a business opportunity and getting others to take on the risks. Franklin and Lamar put in the physical effort; Simeon puts in the sales pitch. Each contributes their part.

Still, this job makes it clear that Franklin has abilities that go beyond the gangster life. He is a skilled driver, knows how to react under pressure and usually keeps more common sense than a good part of the people around him. The problem is that, for now, those qualities are at the service of a business that would hardly show up at a job fair.

---

### 💼 Michael De Santa: An Opportunity With a Record

Meeting Michael De Santa changes Franklin's path. Michael is older, has experience in big scores and knows a criminal world different from that of petty street crime. He also has personal, family and financial problems that seem to have survived several moves and a house with a pool.

Franklin sees in him something he doesn't find in Lamar or Simeon: a possible gateway to larger-scale operations. Michael, for his part, recognizes in Franklin a young man capable of driving, learning and keeping a relatively cool head when everything starts to go wrong.

Their relationship isn't limited to that of an experienced criminal teaching tricks to a beginner. Michael becomes a kind of mentor to Franklin, even if the training program includes heists, chases and an alarming absence of paid internships in an office.

Franklin manages to get closer to the life he imagined, but the path that opens up before him is far from clean. The opportunity comes from someone who knows how to make money from crime and who, despite his experience, hasn't found the formula for living peacefully either.

In Los Santos, moving up a level doesn't necessarily mean leaving problems behind. Sometimes it only means the problems start driving more expensive cars.

---

### 🌅 A Future Yet to Be Decided

Franklin Clinton is the protagonist who looks forward. Michael is trapped between what he achieved and what he lost; Trevor seems determined to turn any situation into a memorable catastrophe. Franklin, on the other hand, is still looking for his place.

He has ambition, skill and a fairly clear idea that the life he leads can't be his final destination. But he is not an exemplary hero who moves ahead without looking back. He drags his past along, keeps ties with people who pull him in different directions and moves through a city that sells success as if wanting it hard enough were all it took.

His story poses a simple question: can someone escape their environment without completely disowning the people who are part of it?

Franklin doesn't need to become someone else in order to progress, but he will have to decide what he is willing to leave behind and what kind of man he wants to be when he finally has the chance to choose.

Because in Los Santos everyone wants to get somewhere. The difference is that some have a plan, others have a car and a few believe that shouting louder than everyone else counts as a strategy.

## Trevor Philips

### The American Dream, but With a Restraining Order

Former soldier. Bank robber. Drug dealer. Businessman. Threat to public order. And, against all odds, one of the few men in San Andreas who still takes the word “loyalty” seriously.

Some people need to hit rock bottom to change their lives. Trevor Philips needs someone to point out where rock bottom is, because he has probably already gone through it, stolen something on the way down and left a corpse as a souvenir.

Trevor is of Canadian origin, a former aspiring military pilot and a professional criminal. He is a man capable of turning an everyday conversation into a death threat and a bar argument into an incident requiring three ambulances, two helicopters and a police press conference.

He lives in Sandy Shores, a dusty town in Blaine County where the sun punishes, opportunities are scarce and the distinction between a troublesome neighbor and a threat to national security is, at best, academic.

Trevor is not simply a madman with a gun. He is an intelligent, extraordinarily dangerous man, with a talent for improvisation, exceptional flying ability and a concept of diplomacy that consists of checking how long it takes the other person to stop arguing.

And yet, behind that spectacle of violence, filth and appalling decisions, there is a story much more human than he would be willing to admit.

---

### 🧸 A Childhood That Didn't Come With a Warranty

Trevor was born in Canada, near the border with the United States. He grew up in a deeply dysfunctional family environment, marked by his father's violence and his mother's emotional control.

His childhood was a succession of homes, moves, conflicts and experiences that don't appear in family tourism brochures. According to his own accounts, he went through numerous houses and foster homes, and had a disastrous relationship with practically any authority figure who crossed his path. From a very young age he showed violent impulses and a monumental difficulty controlling his anger.

Was that childhood the cause of everything that would come afterward? It would be tempting to offer an elegant psychological explanation. But we are talking about Trevor, not a case study from a psychology department.

He also had a brother, Ryan, whose death is mentioned in the game, although it isn't clearly explained under what circumstances it happened.

---

### ✈️ The Pilot He Could Have Been… and the Army Preferred Not to Have

Before becoming a career criminal, Trevor had a surprisingly conventional aspiration: he wanted to fly.

He had a natural talent for piloting aircraft and even joined the Air Force with the intention of becoming a military pilot. For once, he seemed to have found a profession in which his skills could serve a legal purpose.

The problem was Trevor.

His behavior and instability during the psychological evaluation ended his military career before he could complete his training as a combat pilot. The army examined his profile and reached a conclusion that, all things considered, is hard to argue with: putting Trevor in command of a military plane was not the best of ideas.

Aviation, however, never disappeared from his life. Trevor would end up becoming the trusted pilot of his own criminal organization. Because if his career shows anything, it is that professional skills always find an outlet in the “job market”. 

For Michael, the deception was a calculated operation to protect his future. For Trevor, it was a monumental betrayal.

And if there is something Trevor doesn't take well, besides rules, insults and someone touching his things, it is discovering that the person he considered his brother has kept him away from the truth for years.

The bomb was ready. All that was missing was someone to light the fuse.

---

### 🌵 Sandy Shores: An Empire Built on Sand, Meth and Terrible Decisions

Nine years after the North Yankton heist, Trevor lives in Sandy Shores, in Blaine County. His residence is a ramshackle trailer that looks like it lost an argument against the desert and, afterward, against its own owner.

There he runs Trevor Philips Enterprises, a company dedicated to drug and arms trafficking. The name has a certain corporate elegance: it sounds like a respectable multinational, although its business meetings would probably not pass a tax inspection, an ethics audit or a surprise visit from absolutely anyone.

His team includes:

* **Ron Jakowski**: a nervous, paranoid man who seems to live permanently three seconds away from a breakdown.
* **Wade Hebert**: whose innocence and limited ability to understand what is happening around him make him an especially vulnerable companion.
* **Chef**: who collaborates in Trevor's criminal activities.

Trevor runs this little ecosystem with the subtlety of a hurricane. His business model is simple: get merchandise, intimidate the competition, settle conflicts and expand. The catch is that a good part of those operations ends in shootouts, fires or destruction of other people's property.

---

### 💥 Trevor's Rage: When Self-Control Goes on Strike

Trevor's rage is not a simple character trait. It is practically his operating system. He can be calm, joke around or chat with apparent normality, and switch in a matter of seconds to disproportionate violence. He is also extremely sensitive to jokes about his Canadian origin. A trait that, in someone else, might produce a discussion about geography, in Trevor can turn into an incident.

## Michael, Trevor and Franklin: Three Paths to Disaster

### Los Santos, 2013: The Past Knocks on the Door Again

Franklin Clinton is a young man from Los Santos who aspires to escape a life marked by small-time jobs and opportunities that never quite arrive. He works alongside Lamar Davis for Simeon Yetarian, a car salesman whose interpretation of business ethics leaves plenty of room for imagination. The two of them recover vehicles from customers who haven't paid, a job that lets them survive but is hardly going to take them very far.

One of those assignments leads them to the vehicle of Jimmy De Santa, Michael's son. What looked like another routine repossession ends with Franklin discovering that Michael is hiding in the car and pointing a gun at him to force him to drive to the dealership.

The encounter doesn't exactly start with a handshake, but it sparks Michael's interest. Franklin shows that he can handle himself under pressure and that he has more ambition than desire to spend his life running errands for Simeon. Michael sees in him someone with potential, a young man who still hasn't found an opportunity worthy of his aspirations.

Their relationship grows stronger when Michael, after a family conflict, turns to Franklin to solve his problems. Later on, both end up taking part in the jewelry store robbery that Michael organizes with the help of Lester Crest. The job goes through, although it draws police attention that can hardly be considered an added benefit.

And then something happens that Michael had been trying to avoid for almost a decade.

Trevor Philips sees the news about the robbery and recognizes his former partner. Michael is alive.

Since the North Yankton heist in 2004, Trevor had believed that Michael was dead and that Brad Snider was still in prison. Now he discovers that his friend not only survived, but has built a new life in Los Santos, with a family and an identity that have allowed him to keep his past buried.

For Trevor, the discovery changes the rules of the game. He doesn't need a formal invitation or an explanation in advance. If Michael is alive, the time has come to reunite with him and find out what really happened that night.

---

### Three Protagonists, a Worrying Amount of Trouble

With Trevor back in Los Santos, the lives of the three protagonists begin to intertwine. Michael and Trevor meet again after years apart, while Franklin goes from being a young man looking for opportunities to becoming part of much bigger operations.

Michael knows the world of big heists and wants to keep control of his new life, although his own decisions push him again and again toward the past he is trying to escape. Trevor brings experience, contacts and an extraordinary ability to turn any setback into an emergency of state-wide proportions. Franklin, for his part, brings skill behind the wheel, pragmatism and an ambition that still allows him to imagine a different future.

The possibility of taking part in big scores together again represents for Trevor the chance to recover the partner with whom he shared his criminal life. For Michael, it means getting close again to a life he swore to leave behind. Franklin, meanwhile, sees the possibility of an economic leap that you don't get by filling out job applications.

However, working together again doesn't mean regaining lost trust. Between Michael and Trevor there is a history that neither of them can erase, and the reunion threatens to bring to light everything Michael has spent years trying to hide.

---

### The North Yankton Grave: The Truth Nobody Wanted to Find

The reunion with Michael isn't enough to close the wounds of the past. As Trevor begins to question what happened in North Yankton, the version he has accepted for almost a decade falls apart. Brad is supposedly still in prison, but Michael is alive. If the pieces don't fit, an inevitable question remains: what really happened during that heist?

The doubts take Trevor back to Ludendorff, where he goes to the cemetery to open Michael's grave. His former partner tries to talk him out of it, but Trevor goes ahead. When the coffin is opened, he finds Brad's remains instead of Michael's.

The lie is exposed. Michael had reached a secret agreement with Dave Norton to fake his death and escape his old life. During the 2004 ambush, Brad died by stepping into the path of a shot aimed at Trevor. Afterward, his body was buried under Michael's name, while Trevor escaped believing that his partner had died and that Brad was still in prison.

For Trevor, that is not a simple deception. It is the confirmation that the man he considered his friend and partner abandoned him while he lived for years with a false version of events. His rage doesn't stem solely from the loss of Brad, but also from discovering that the loyalty he had placed in Michael was repaid with a carefully maintained lie.

The truth has come to light, but that doesn't mean things are going to get fixed. Michael and Trevor are still alive, although their friendship is going through one of its most fragile moments. Franklin, who took no part in the original deception, now finds himself tied to the consequences of a betrayal that began long before he met Michael.

What unites these three men is not a perfect friendship, but a shared history of ambition, deceit, loyalties and decisions that are hard to come out of unscathed. In Los Santos, where everyone is chasing money, power or a second chance, surviving your own mistakes can be quite a bit more complicated than making them.

titulo: Lester Crest: The Mastermind in the Shadows
subtitulo: The heist planner · Hacker, strategist and the man who pulls the strings from the couch

## 🧠 Lester Crest

### The Planner Who Never Sets Foot at the Crime Scene

In any well-organized heist there is someone who shoots, someone who drives and someone who makes sure everything goes according to plan. **Lester Crest** is the third. He doesn't wield a gun, doesn't flee by car and, if he can avoid it, doesn't even get up from the couch. His working tools are a computer, a prodigious memory and a distrust of the world that, given the events, turns out to be quite reasonable.

Without Lester, the three protagonists of GTA V would still be a retired thief, a meth dealer and a kid with a car. With Lester, they become a team capable of planning scores that other criminals only dare to dream of.

---

### 💻 The Old Crew's Hacker

Lester's history with Michael is older than it seems. In 2004 he was already part of the circle of Michael Townley, Trevor Philips and Brad Snider, working with them as a hacker on several of their jobs in North Yankton. He was the technical brain of a group in which the others provided brute force and marksmanship.

All of that ended when the Ludendorff heist was interrupted by the FIB and the crew fell apart. Each went their own way: Michael disappeared with a new identity, Trevor got lost in the desert, and Lester settled in Los Santos to keep moving along the margins of the criminal world.

---

### 🏠 A Bungalow in El Burro Heights

In Los Santos, Lester earned a reputation as someone who knew everything that moved in the world of heists: who is planning what, who has money and who is in trouble. Information, in short, the most valuable currency in a city that boasts of having no secrets and sells them separately.

His daily life takes place in a bungalow in El Burro Heights, surrounded by screens. A degenerative illness has limited his mobility for years: in 2013 he is still able to walk, although with difficulty, and he relies on a cane or a wheelchair depending on the day. His body sets limits for him, but his mind doesn't recognize them.

Lester also has the habit of keeping an eye on his friends, reading their emails and finding out everything that happens to them before they do. It is a rather peculiar form of affection, although it's best not to ask him how he finds out what he finds out.

---

### 🧵 The Darnell Bros. Factory: The Legal Business That Isn't Quite So Legal

As if the résumé weren't interesting enough, in 2013 Lester runs the Darnell Bros. textile factory, where Guadalupe Romero works. On paper, he is a businessman in the garment sector. In practice, the factory serves as a perfect cover and a discreet headquarters.

Working conditions seem to leave quite a lot to be desired: at the end of 2013 production stops again because of labor disputes, and two union representatives even show up asking for him. Lester, like any exemplary businessman, prefers not to be available.

---

### 🤝 The Reunion With Michael

Lester and Michael cross paths again when Michael urgently needs money after his confrontation with Martin Madrazo. Lester agrees to help him, but first sets a condition: the mission **Friend Request**. The plan consists of tampering with a Lifeinvader phone prototype so that the company's founder, Jay Norris, suffers a fatal accident during a televised presentation. Lester has his reasons and doesn't share them much.

With that debt settled, Lester plans the first big score with Michael: **the Vangelico jewelry store robbery**. It is here that he meets Franklin, and where the idea of a team begins to take shape.

---

### 📈 Franklin, the Stock Market and Lester's Assignments

Lester sees in Franklin someone with the qualities necessary for more than repossessing cars. He assigns him a series of assassinations of executives and corrupt figures whose disappearance directly affects the stock market value of their companies. Lester, meanwhile, invests with that knowledge in advance.

Among Franklin's targets are:

* **Bret Lowrey**, director of Betta Pharmaceuticals.
* **Four jury members** corrupted in a trial against Redwood Cigarettes.
* **Jackson Skinner**, head of development at Facade.
* **Isaac Penny**, an investor who laid off employees to manipulate a company's value.
* **Enzo Bonelli**, a former criminal turned real estate developer.

The business goes well. Lester ends up buying Franklin a house in Vinewood Hills with part of the profits.

* If you want to make the most of these assignments, check the Stock Market chapter: the moment you buy and sell makes the difference.

---

### 🏦 The Brain Behind the Big Heists

As the plot advances, Lester becomes the centerpiece of the team. He plans the Paleto bank job, prepares the raid on the FIB building and designs the big score at the Union Depository, the biggest of all. He also helps locate Michael when he is kidnapped in Ludendorff and collaborates in the rescue of Lamar when the Ballas capture him.

* Lester **does not take part in the Merryweather assault**: he knows Trevor has located Michael and prefers to stay out of the plan.
* His relationship with Trevor is the coldest in the group. They have known each other for years, and precisely for that reason he prefers to keep his distance.
* With his share of the loot, Lester retires from the textile business and plans to improve his bungalow.

---

### 🎬 Character Details

* Lester is played by the actor Jay Klaitz.
* It has been suggested that the character may be inspired by Kelso, from the movie *Heat* (1995): he is also physically limited and takes part in the planning, not the execution.

---

### 🕸️ The Man Who Knows Everything

Lester is proof that in Los Santos power doesn't always belong to whoever shouts the loudest or shoots first. Sometimes it belongs to whoever sits calmly in front of a screen, knows where everything is and lets others deal with the uncomfortable details. While Michael, Trevor and Franklin risk their lives, Lester risks boredom. And yet, he is probably the only one who always knows how each job will end before it begins.

titulo: Lamar Davis: The Loyal and Reckless Homeboy
subtitulo: The heart of Chamberlain Hills · Gangs, blind loyalty and plans doomed to disaster
contenidoMarkdown:
## 🟢 Lamar Davis

### The King of the Hood Who Never Leaves It

If you ask **Lamar Davis**, he'll tell you he is one step away from conquering the street business of Los Santos, that his business vision has no rival and that true respect is earned by representing the Chamberlain Gangster Families. If you ask anyone who has known him for more than five minutes, they'll confirm that he is a guy with overflowing charisma, bulletproof loyalty and an astonishing ability to walk straight into deadly ambushes that others have to shoot him out of.

Lamar is the perfect counterpoint to Franklin Clinton: while Franklin seeks to escape the neighborhood loop and dreams of making the leap to the upper echelons, Lamar feels comfortable in the mud, embracing gang culture with unshakable pride and an impulsiveness that knows nothing of escape plans.

---

### 🧢 Roots in Davis and a Lifelong Friendship

Born and raised in the troubled district of Davis, in South Los Santos, Lamar grew up on the same streets as Franklin, Tanisha Jackson and Tonya Wiggins. Unlike Franklin —who was expelled from high school after a violent altercation— Lamar frequently brags about having graduated, although the diploma didn't keep him from petty crime, robberies and neighborhood dealing.

His relationship with Franklin goes far beyond a simple gang friendship: they are practically brothers. They tell each other the most hurtful truths without filters —like his legendary jokes about Franklin's haircut—, argue over any stupidity and have opposite views of life, but when things really go wrong, Lamar doesn't hesitate for a second to put his neck on the line for his friend.

---

### 🚘 Repossessions With Simeon and the Dog Chop

At the beginning of the story, Lamar and Franklin work as vehicle repossession specialists for Simeon Yetarian at the Premium Deluxe Motorsport dealership. For Lamar, repossessing cars bought on credit from people who can't pay for them is just a temporary step toward his own empire.

It is also during this stage that Lamar acquires **Chop**, an imposing Rottweiler that originally belonged to his associate Darnell. Lamar involves Franklin and the dog in the harebrained kidnapping of D, a member of the Ballas, an operation that ends in an absolute fiasco when he uses his own cell phone to demand the ransom, forcing them to let him go and leaving Franklin permanently in charge of Chop.

---

### ⚠️ The Permanent Trap of Stretch and the Ballas

Lamar's greatest weakness is his naivety regarding street loyalty. When Harold “Stretch” Joseph gets out of prison, Lamar welcomes him as a hero and neighborhood mentor. Franklin is suspicious from the first minute, but Lamar trusts blindly.

That blind faith drags the group into one trap after another set by Stretch in collusion with the Ballas:

* **The recycling plant**: a supposed drug deal that turns into a death trap which Franklin, Lamar and Stretch barely escape alive.
* **Grove Street (Hood Safari)**: a cocaine exchange alongside Trevor and Franklin that turns out to be a plaster brick and sets off a massive shootout in the heart of Ballas territory.
* **The Paleto Forest sawmill**: blinded by his desire to prove his worth on his own, Lamar travels north to buy drugs from the Ballas, where he is captured and tied up awaiting execution.

The rescue at the sawmill (**Lamar Down**) marks one of the high points of the story: Franklin has to turn to both Michael and Trevor to organize a large-scale assault with rifles and snipers to save Lamar from certain death.

---

### 🎬 Character Details

* Lamar is played by the actor and comedian **Slink Johnson**, whose chemistry and improvisations in the recording booth brought to life the comic and shameless tone of the character.
* Despite his constant stumbles, Lamar is one of the few characters in the GTA V universe who shows unconditional loyalty: he doesn't hesitate to show up with his van to back Franklin and his partners at the foundry when everything is decided in the story.

---

### 🟢 The Unquenchable Spirit of South Los Santos

Lamar Davis is loud, reckless and a genuine magnet for trouble, but he also represents authenticity in a city where almost everyone wears a mask. He doesn't pretend to be a refined guy or hide who he is. In a world of government betrayals and corrupt businessmen, Lamar's wild and selfless loyalty is one of the few certainties Franklin has left when the shooting intensifies.

titulo: The De Santa Family: Amanda, Jimmy and Tracey
subtitulo: The American dream in ruins behind the Rockford Hills fence
contenidoMarkdown:
## 🍷 The De Santa Family: The Rockford Hills Circus

To get a professional bank robber to retire to a mansion with a pool in Rockford Hills, the government promised Michael Townley the great American dream. What nobody warned him about in the protection contract is that daily life with **Amanda, Jimmy and Tracey** would turn out to be infinitely more wearing than any shootout with the FIB.

The De Santas are the ultimate satire of contemporary suburban bourgeoisie: a family where therapy is a sterile formality, communication boils down to shouting from door to door and Dad's credit card is the only mortar holding up the foundations of the home.

---

### 🎾 Amanda De Santa: Tennis, Yoga and Marital Resentment

A former stripper in Michael's wild years in the Midwest, **Amanda** traded dressing rooms for the luxury shops of Portola Drive, where she spends lavishly to drown the bitterness of a broken marriage. Convinced that Michael is an insensitive monster addicted to violence, Amanda doesn't hesitate to seek comfort in the arms of any instructor who sets foot in her garden.

* **The plot's trigger**: her affair with the conceited tennis coach, Kyle Chavis, unleashes Michael's fury. By chasing him to a residence in the hills and tearing down the structure of the mansion together with Franklin, Michael discovers that the property belonged to the drug trafficker Martin Madrazo, forcing him out of retirement to pay off the million-dollar debt.
* **The yoga teacher**: her obsession with spiritual refinement throws her into the hands of Fabien LaRouche, a pedantic instructor whose intimate poses end with Michael losing his temper and throwing Fabien headfirst into the family pool.

---

### 🎮 Jimmy “J-Dog” De Santa: The Couch Parasite

At a little over twenty, **James “Jimmy” De Santa** embodies the caricature of the unproductive young man of the digital age. Shut in his dark room, Jimmy divides his days between marijuana joints, headband headphones, marathons of war video games like *Righteous Slaughter 7* and internet forums where he invents a neighborhood gangster life he has never set foot in.

* **The yacht fiasco**: in his attempt to act as an independent street dealer, Jimmy tries to sell Michael's private yacht to a group of thugs. The operation turns into an express kidnapping along the highway from which Franklin and Michael must rescue him while the boat is towed at full speed.
* **The drug betrayal**: fed up with his father's lectures, Jimmy goes to the extreme of drugging Michael's coffee with a powerful anesthetic, stealing his car, emptying his bank account and abandoning him in his underwear in an alley, marking the total break and the family's exodus from the mansion.

---

### ⭐ Tracey De Santa: Fame, Cameras and Secondhand Embarrassment

The eldest daughter, **Tracey**, lives obsessed with instant celebrity culture and social media. Desperate to appear on television and escape her mother's shadow, Tracey is willing to tolerate any public humiliation in order to get her fifteen minutes of fame.

* **Fame or Shame**: Tracey's audition for the talent show hosted by the lecherous Lazlow Jones pushes Michael and a newly arrived Trevor Philips to burst onto the set, chase Lazlow through the river canals and force him to dance in his underwear at gunpoint to protect the girl's dignity.
* **The Vinewood stalkers**: despite her constant snubs of her father, Michael must step in on several occasions as her personal bodyguard, keeping away depraved producers and dangerous admirers who lurk around the house.

---

### 🤝 The Catharsis: “Reuniting the Family”

The clan's turning point comes when the home hits rock bottom and everyone abandons Michael. After months apart, Jimmy arranges a meeting at the upscale restaurant *Bean Machine*. What begins as an attempt at family mediation with Dr. Friedlander and the conceited Fabien ends with a cathartic fight that clears the air:

* Amanda understands that, despite his brutal flaws, Michael is the only real shield between her family and the city's criminals.
* Jimmy begins to mature, exercising and looking for a job.
* Tracey decides to focus on her college studies.

When the Merryweather mercenaries storm the Rockford Hills mansion during the premiere of *Meltdown*, the De Santas act like a truly coordinated team: Michael takes down the attackers while Jimmy neutralizes an armed mercenary with a well-placed blow to the back of the head, sealing the definitive reconciliation of the most chaotic household in Los Santos.

titulo: Trevor's Circle: Ron Jakowski and Wade Hebert
subtitulo: Conspiracy-theory paranoia and absolute submission in the Blaine County desert
contenidoMarkdown:
## 🛢️ The Blaine County Entourage: Ron and Wade

Surviving in the shadow of Trevor Philips in the radioactive dust of Sandy Shores requires one of two qualities: either an extreme paranoia that keeps you in a constant state of alert, or an innocence so anesthetized that it keeps you from understanding the danger of being half a meter from a grenade with the pin pulled. Those two faces are represented by **“Nervous” Ron Jakowski** and **Wade Hebert**, the only two stable collaborators of the most improvised criminal corporation in the state: **Trevor Philips Enterprises**.

Far from being business partners on equal terms, Ron and Wade are Trevor's shock entourage: the first handles communications while trembling like a leaf, and the second acts as a street bloodhound without being aware that his own family will end up paying the price of his loyalty.

---

### 📻 “Nervous” Ron Jakowski: Paranoia Turned Lieutenant

Trevor's trailer neighbor and unofficial co-owner of his businesses, **Ron** is a textbook conspiracy theorist. He firmly believes in aliens abducting farmers, in the government adding chemicals to tap water to control the population and in the New World Order watching his every move through spy satellites. His refuge is his nightly pirate radio show (*Blaine County Community Radio*), from which he broadcasts apocalyptic rants between swigs of homemade liquor.

* **The terrified partner**: Ron's relationship with Trevor is a toxic mix of blind admiration and paralyzing terror. Ron refers to him almost as a deity of violence, putting up with slaps, threats of dismemberment and daily insults with an almost reverential submission.
* **The Sandy Shores Airfield assault**: despite his chronic hand tremor, Ron proves to be an indispensable military asset. In the mission *Nervous Ron*, he is the one who handles the logistics and assists Trevor with the sniper rifle to eradicate The Lost MC bikers from the landing strip, securing the airfield and piloting smuggling planes with surprising skill.

---

### 🤡 Wade Hebert: Innocence in War Paint

With a *juggalo* look, unkempt dreadlocks and a brain seriously damaged by abusive drug use, **Wade** is the embodiment of childlike innocence trapped in a scruffy adult body. Years ago, Wade arrived in Sandy Shores with his childhood friends; after running into Trevor in the desert, his companions “mysteriously disappeared” (victims of Trevor himself), and Wade was adopted as a helpful pet who never asks uncomfortable questions.

* **Michael's bloodhound**: Trevor's entire plot gets reactivated thanks to Wade. After hearing that the Vangelico jewelry store robber uttered an exact phrase of his old friend presumed dead, Trevor entrusts Wade with the task of combing through the Los Santos records. Despite his clumsiness, Wade finds the trail of Michael Townley under the last name De Santa.
* **Floyd's tragedy in La Puerta**: Wade guides Trevor to his cousin Floyd Hebert's apartment in Vespucci Beach to use it as an operations base for the Merryweather port assault. While Floyd lives through a genuine psychological nightmare, Wade remains oblivious to everything.
* **The golden retirement at the Vanilla Unicorn**: after the bloody outcome in Floyd and Debra's apartment, Trevor diverts Wade's attention to keep him from discovering the bodies of his cousin and his partner. He takes him to the strip club *Vanilla Unicorn*, where he pays two dancers to entertain him and look after him in a private booth, and there Wade stays happy and isolated for the rest of the story.

---

### ⚖️ The Glue of Trevor Philips Enterprises

Trevor humiliates, beats and manipulates Ron and Wade daily, but paradoxically doesn't destroy them. In Trevor Philips' twisted code of loyalty, both are “his people”: useful tools, but also the only living beings who have neither judged nor betrayed him. In a ruthless world where partners sell out to the highest bidder for a handful of dollars, Ron and Wade represent loyalty born of need, fear and the purest emotional dependence in the heart of the desert.

titulo: The FIB Agents: Dave Norton and Steve Haines
subtitulo: Federal hypocrisy between comfortable pragmatism and television megalomania
contenidoMarkdown:
## 🏛️ The Law to the Highest Bidder: Dave Norton and Steve Haines

If there is one institution in Los Santos capable of competing in criminality and shamelessness with any street gang or drug cartel, it is the local branch of the **FIB (Federal Investigation Bureau)**. Through **Dave Norton** and **Steve Haines**, GTA V draws a scathing caricature of the state security apparatus: corrupt bureaucrats, dirty wars between government agencies funded with black money and covert operations that would make any common criminal blush.

Although both wear suits and carry a federal badge, they embody two diametrically opposed ways of handling public immorality.

---

### ☕ Dave Norton: The Pragmatic Civil Servant Who Only Wanted to Retire in Peace

David “Dave” Norton doesn't dream of saving the free world or eradicating organized crime; his true vocation was always much more down-to-earth: to keep a six-figure public salary, stay out of trouble with internal affairs and reach retirement age in one piece. With a weary sarcasm and an almost comic resignation, Dave acts as a permanent firefighter between psychopathic robbers and megalomaniac bosses.

* **The North Yankton pact (2004)**: Dave's brilliant career wasn't forged through risky police raids, but thanks to the most profitable corrupt deal in the Bureau's history. After secretly striking a deal with Michael Townley, he orchestrated the shootout in Ludendorff, shot Brad Snider instead of Trevor and allowed Michael to fake his death. Dave took credit for having brought down America's “public enemy number one”, collected monthly commissions from Michael for a decade and rose through the federal ranks without breaking a sweat.
* **The cornered negotiator**: when the Vangelico jewelry store robbery resurrects the ghost of Michael, Dave understands in panic that if Trevor discovers the truth or the agency investigates Brad's corpse, both will end up in a federal cell or a clandestine grave. His life becomes a continuous comic balancing act, trying to calm a hysterical Michael while begging him to do “patriotic favors” to cover up loose ends.

---

### 📺 Steve Haines: The Media Monster With a God Complex

If Dave is bureaucratic laziness personified, Special Agent **Steve Haines** is the nuclear fuel of arrogance. Young, relentless, narcissistic and decorated to the point of absurdity, Haines uses his FIB badge not as a tool of justice, but as a springboard for his true ambition: to become a national media star as the host of the sensationalist reality show *The Underbelly of Paradise*.

* **The dirty war with the IAA**: upon learning of the North Yankton farce, Haines arrests neither Dave nor Michael; he decides to extort them for his own benefit. He uses the trio (Michael, Franklin and Trevor) as his private black-ops commando to systematically sabotage his rival agency, the IAA (the parody of the CIA), stealing funds, raiding chemical weapons labs and infiltrating skyscrapers in broad daylight.
* **Contempt and megalomania**: convinced that criminals are mere cockroaches he can step on and discard at will, Haines ignores the basic rule of survival in Los Santos: never give orders to an armed psychopath. He treats Trevor with excessive arrogance and blackmails Michael with ruining his family without imagining that he is signing his own death sentence.

---

### 💥 The Chaos at Kortz Center and the Final Fate

The point of no return for both agents erupts at the **Kortz Center**. In a meeting on the terrace to settle the matter, Haines and Norton get caught up in a four-way massacre between the FIB, the IAA and the Merryweather mercenaries. Haines is wounded in the leg and flees cowardly, leaving Dave at the mercy of the crossfire, from which he only manages to escape alive thanks to the timely intervention of Michael and Trevor's sniper rifle.

* **Steve Haines' fate**: drunk on impunity, Haines films a new episode of his show aboard the Ferris wheel at Del Perro Pier. There, Trevor Philips —posted hundreds of meters away with a precision rifle— puts a fatal shot through him live in front of the cameras, abruptly ending his television and ministerial career.
* **Dave's golden retirement**: with Haines out of the equation and the accounts settled, Dave Norton demonstrates why the prudent civil servant always outlives the ambitious one. In the epilogue of the story, Dave definitively closes Michael's file, cuts his ties with the underworld and assures his old friend that he will keep a low profile, proving that in Los Santos crime doesn't pay... unless you have an FIB badge.

titulo: Devin Weston: The Great Corporate Shark
subtitulo: Megalomania, venture capital and the impunity of the one percent
contenidoMarkdown:
## 💼 Devin Weston: The Depravity of Venture Capital

If Steve Haines represents the blatant abuse of police power, **Devin Weston** embodies something much more dangerous: the absolute power of money in a system where laws are merely negotiable suggestions for billionaires. At the head of *Devin Weston Holdings* and majority shareholder of the all-powerful private military corporation **Merryweather Security**, Weston is the perfect caricature of the 21st-century corporate shark: he talks about Eastern spirituality while exploiting child labor, wears designer athletic spandex in executive meetings and practices yoga poses to “align his chakras” before ordering a targeted assassination.

For Weston, morality or loyalty are pathologies of the poor; people are not human beings, but mere depreciable assets on a balance sheet.

---

### 🏎️ The Luxury Supercar Scam

Introduced to the group by Steve Haines, Weston immediately sees in Franklin Clinton and Trevor Philips the ideal pawns to feed his collector's whim without paying a single dollar through legal means. Under the promise of a million-dollar payoff that will change Franklin's life, he hires them to steal the most coveted cars in the state (among them a Pegassi Monroe, a Grotti Cheetah and a JB 700 with spy accessories):

* **Posing as police officers**: Franklin and Trevor ride highway patrol motorcycles to seize vehicles at high speed.
* **The corporate economics lesson**: when Franklin and Trevor deliver the last convoy in the north of Paleto Bay and claim their pay, Weston gives them a mocking smile. He explains condescendingly that paying in cash “is for middle-class losers” and that their money has been reinvested in shares managed by his firm. The protagonists instantly understand that they have been used and swindled by the financial elite.

---

### 🎬 The Vinewood Conflict and Molly's Tragedy

The direct clash with Michael De Santa arises on the Vinewood film sets. Fascinated by cinema, Michael works as an associate producer on Solomon Richards' classic *Meltdown*. Weston, majority partner of the Richards Majestic studios, plans to cancel the premiere and destroy the original copies in order to collect a multimillion-dollar insurance payout:

* **The deadly chase at the airport**: Michael rescues the film and chases Devin's personal lawyer, **Molly Schultz**, to a hangar at Los Santos International Airport. Panicking and fleeing with the film reel, Molly recklessly approaches the running turbine of a private jet and dies, sucked in and torn into a thousand pieces before Michael's astonished eyes.
* **The vendetta with Merryweather**: Weston blames Michael for the loss of his valuable lawyer and orchestrates a savage reprisal: he hires the Merryweather mercenaries to storm the Rockford Hills mansion during the red carpet of the *Meltdown* premiere, seeking to annihilate Amanda and her children.

---

### ⛰️ The Outcome: The Trip in the Trunk

Devin Weston's arrogance digs his own grave in the final stretch of the story. Believing himself untouchable because of his status as a tycoon and his private security, Weston shows up at Franklin's hill to give him an ultimatum: kill Michael (Option B) or face the consequences.

In the canonical ending (**Option C: The Third Way**), Franklin rejects the order and seals the billionaire's fate:

* Trevor Philips single-handedly storms Weston's fortified mansion in Richman, wipes out the contingent of elite Merryweather guards and finds Weston hiding in his underwear inside a wicker chest by the pool.
* Trevor knocks him out, locks him in the trunk of his own brand-new roadster and drives to the desert cliffs of Paleto Cove, meeting up with Michael and Franklin.
* After reminding him that in Los Santos nobody buys eternal impunity, the three protagonists push the car off the precipice. The vehicle crashes against the rocks and explodes in a fireball over the ocean waves, putting an end to the empire of San Andreas' greatest corporate villain.

subtitulo: Everything strictly necessary to unlock the 100% statistic and the Criminal Career achievement
contenidoMarkdown:
## 🏆 Summary of Requirements for 100%

To reach 100% in GTA V's Stats tab you don't need to do absolutely every side mission in the game, but rather meet the following Rockstar Games checklist:

---

### 1. Main Campaign Missions (69 missions)
* Complete the **69 main story missions**, including all the planned heists from the Prologue in North Yankton to the story's conclusion.
* The choice of tactical approach (Stealth or Brute Force) or the chosen ending doesn't prevent reaching 100%.

---

### 2. Strangers and Freaks (20 of 58 missions)
Only **Franklin Clinton's** missions count, since Michael and Trevor have optional missions that don't block the trophy:
* **Tonya**: The 5 tow truck missions in Los Santos.
* **Beverly**: All the paparazzi and celebrity-chasing missions.
* **Hao**: The initial street race that unlocks the night competitions.
* **Barry**: Franklin's exclusive legalization missions.
* **Mary-Ann**: The triathlon race and foot chase with Franklin.
* **Dom**: The 4 extreme skydiving challenges.
* **Omega**: Collect the 50 spaceship parts (unlocks the Space Docker vehicle).
* **Dreyfuss**: Collect the 50 letter scraps and solve the murder of Leonora Johnson.

---

### 3. Hobbies and Pastimes (42 activities)
* **Golf**: Win a 9-hole match finishing at par or under par.
* **Tennis**: Win a full set against the AI or a friend.
* **Darts**: Win a full game at the Yellow Jack Inn or Los Santos bar.
* **Triathlons**: Complete the 3 triathlons (including the big Lago Zancudo Triathlon).
* **Shooting Range**: Complete all the shooting challenges with at least a bronze medal in each weapon type.
* **Flight School**: Pass the 12 Los Santos International Flight School tests.
* **Street Races**: Win the 5 night car races.
* **Off-Road Races**: Win the 6 off-road races through the desert and the mountains.
* **Sea Races**: Win the 4 boat races.
* **Strip Club**: Get a private dance from a dancer.
* **Skydiving**: Complete all the base jumps and helicopter jumps in the city.

---

### 4. Random Events (14 events)
* Witness and successfully resolve at least **14 of the 57 random events** spread across Los Santos and Blaine County (such as muggings, ATM thieves or hitchhikers).

---

### 5. Miscellaneous and Exploration (16 activities)
* Buy at least **5 properties** that generate weekly income.
* Buy a vehicle over the Internet on the cell phone (Eyefind).
* Collect the **50 spaceship parts**.
* Collect the **50 Leonora Johnson mystery letters**.
* Perform **25 of the 50 unique Stunt Jumps**.
* Perform **8 of the 15 Under the Bridge Flights**.
* Perform **8 of the 15 Knife Flights** between the downtown skyscrapers.
* Go to the movies and watch a full film.
* Go out for a walk and throw the ball with **Chop** using Franklin.

titulo: Tactical Guide to the 6 Major Heists
subtitulo: Choice of plans and optimal crew
contenidoMarkdown:
## 💰 Tactical Guide to the 6 Major Heists

The Heists are the core of GTA V's story. Each one lets you choose between two tactical approaches and hire support crew members (Gunmen, Drivers and Hackers).

> **Key Crew Tip**: Rookie members gain skill with every heist without asking for a larger cut. Hiring rookies with a low starting percentage maximizes your earnings in the final heists.

---

### 1. The Vangelico Jewelry Store Heist
* **Recommended Approach**: **Plan A (Stealth)**. Using BZ gas through the ventilation ducts gives you more time in the store without immediately facing the police.
* **Hacker**: **Rickie Lukens** (4% cut after helping him at Lifeinvader). He gives you 3 minutes and 30 seconds, enough to empty all the display cases.
* **Driver**: **Karim Denz** (8%). Choose the Bagger bikes; even if he gets it wrong in the Los Santos river tunnels, you won't lose loot.
* **Gunman**: **Packie McReary** (12%, unlockable in a random event in Strawberry) or **Norm Richards** (7%).

---

### 2. The Merryweather Heist
* **Approach**: **Plan A (Cargobob / Open sea)** or **Plan B (Submarine / Freighter)**.
* **Net Loot**: **$0** (Lester discovers that the superweapon is property of the U.S. government and must be returned to avoid federal pursuit).

---

### 3. The Paleto Bay Heist
* **Approach**: Frontal assault with Juggernaut armored suits and Minigun rotary machine guns.
* **Gunman**: **Chef** (12%) or **Packie McReary** (12%). They will keep the SWAT at bay without dying or losing money from the bag.
* **Gross Loot**: ~$8,000,000 (decreases every time the police shoot at your back).

---

### 4. The Humane Labs Raid
* **Objective**: Recover the nerve toxin for Steve Haines and Dave Norton.
* **Preparation**: Obtain the neurotoxic gas and escape through the underwater vents with diving suits.

---

### 5. The FIB Building Raid
* **Recommended Approach**: **Plan B (Rooftop entry / Skydiving)**. You avoid disguising yourselves as firefighters and the shootout is much more direct and clean.
* **Hacker**: **Rickie Lukens** (4%) to shut down the firewalls quickly.

---

### 6. The Big Score (Union Depository)
* **Recommended Approach**: **Plan A (Subtle / Traffic)** or **Plan B (Front drill)**.
* **Driver 1**: **Karim Denz** (8%) if he has already taken part in earlier heists and has his skill maxed out.
* **Driver 2**: **Taliana Martinez** (5%, rescuable on the highway north of Sandy Shores). She is the best driver in the game and only asks for 5%.
* **Maximum Loot**: Around **$201,600,000 in gold bars** (~$35,000,000 net for each protagonist).

subtitulo: Decisions and consequences of the story's ending
contenidoMarkdown:
## 🎭 The Three Endings: Option A, B or C

At the end of the Big Score mission, Franklin Clinton is visited by Devin Weston and Steve Haines, forcing him to make an irrevocable decision about his loyalty:

---

### Option A: Kill Trevor (Something Sensible)
* Franklin chases Trevor to the oil tanks in El Burro Heights. Michael intervenes by ramming Trevor's van into a fuel tank.
* Trevor dies engulfed in flames. Franklin and Michael drift apart forever. You lose Trevor and all his money.

---

### Option B: Kill Michael (The Time's Come)
* Franklin arranges to meet Michael on the city limits. After a chase through a power plant, Michael hangs from a metal tower.
* Michael dies after falling into the void. Trevor cuts off any relationship with Franklin, disowning him as a traitor. You lose Michael and his fortune.

---

### Option C: The Third Way (The Canonical Ending)
* Franklin looks for Lester to devise a plan: unite the three protagonists in an abandoned foundry to ambush both the Merryweather agents and the FIB ones.
* **The Coordinated Executions**:
  * Trevor travels to Del Perro Pier and kills **Steve Haines** while he films his show on the Ferris wheel.
  * Michael infiltrates Chumash and eliminates **Stretch**.
  * Franklin ambushes the Chinese triad and eliminates **Wei Cheng** in Pacific Bluffs.
  * The three capture **Devin Weston** in his mansion, lock him in the trunk of his own car and push it off the cliff into the Pacific Ocean.
* **Consequences**: All three protagonists survive, keep their Big Score loot and remain available to play in Los Santos.
